vBRIEFInfo.description: Story vBRIEF for #2110 (consumer xbrief migration surface); part of the #2034 decomposition.

plan.title: Consumer migration surface: migrate:xbrief verb, update trigger, doctor signpost

narratives.Description: Ship the consumer-facing detect, signpost, and mutate triad for the xbrief rename. This story is independently buildable on top of the migration module: it wires a new CLI verb, a doctor signpost line, and the update-trigger behavior without changing the transform internals.
narratives.ImplementationPlan: 1. Add the packages/cli/src/migrate-xbrief.ts verb that calls the xbrief-migrate module behind a clean-tree gate (mirroring checkGitClean) with a force override. 2. Add a renderXbriefMigrationLine signpost to packages/cli/src/doctor.ts and wire detection into packages/core/src/install-upgrade/index.ts so update signposts by default, migrates under --migrate, and stays inert on patch upgrades; cover each path with cli tests.
narratives.UserStory: As a consumer, I want deft to detect a legacy layout and offer migrate:xbrief, so that I can convert to xbrief safely on my own schedule without silent mutation.

items.title: Given a legacy tree, when deft update runs, then it signposts without mutating by default

narrative.Acceptance: Given a consumer legacy vbrief tree, when deft update runs without flags, then it prints the migrate:xbrief signpost and makes no file changes.

items.title: Given a dirty tree, when migrate:xbrief runs, then it refuses unless force is passed

narrative.Acceptance: Given a dirty working tree, when migrate:xbrief or update --migrate runs, then the command refuses with guidance unless --force is supplied.

items.title: Given a patch upgrade, when deft update runs, then it never mutates or hard-errors

narrative.Acceptance: Given a patch-version deft update on a legacy tree, when it runs, then it emits at most a signpost and never mutates or escalates to a hard error.

expected_outputs: migrate:xbrief verb + doctor signpost + update trigger with clean-tree gate and patch-inert behavior
